title: AutoOS AI model registry
description: Single hand-edited model file (docs/plans/2026-09-25-routing-v2-spec.md section 3, D11). The old catalog/config files and the one-shot converter tools/registry-convert.py were deleted in task A5e; this file is the only hand-edited source. Sections: providers, models, routes, clients, policy - exactly section 3.1's list. Measured values (probes, recalibrate) never write this file; they live in the git-ignored overlay logs/routing/measured.json.

version.description: Registry content date (YYYY-MM-DD), bumped on every hand edit to this file.

providers.description: One entry per upstream provider (spec 3.1). Keyed by provider id (normally also its api-keys.yml name, e.g. 'google_ai_studio'; 'antigravity' and 'cc' are OAuth/subscription bridges with no api-keys.yml entry; a provider that reuses another's key says so with key_name).

models.description: One entry per upstream model (spec 3.1). Keyed by the exact model-id spelling a route leg uses after its provider prefix (providers spell the same real model differently - e.g. groq's 'openai/gpt-oss-120b' vs cerebras's 'gpt-oss-120b' - so those are two distinct entries; see docs/plans/2026-09-25-registry-mapping.md Open choices).

routes.description: One entry per combo / fallback group / pinned single-model route (spec 3.1). Keyed by route id (== configuration/omniroute/combos.json combo name, or the catalog/ide-models.json id for surfaces with no combos.json equivalent).

clients.description: One entry per agent CLI (spec 3.1): opencode, claude, qwen, gemini, codex, agy, qoder.

comment.description: Prose that belongs with the data next to it (D9/D20: don't lose a measured fact). A single line or a list of lines, same convention as the old catalogs' $comment arrays.

source_tag.description: D20: default (unmeasured), probe (overlay-measured), or the ISO date a measurement/decision was made.

until_tag.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant, e.g. "2026-10-01T09:05:00Z" (pattern-checked here; parseability is enforced by tools/registry.py check rule 7).

sourced_number.description: The one consistent shape (D20) for a policy number that is not itself a data table: the value plus where it came from.

window.description: providers.<id>.windows entry (spec 6.4). price_factor is a multiplier on the baseline price (1.0 = no change); kind distinguishes a genuine price window (DeepSeek) from an informational load window (Anthropic/Meta busy hours, price_factor 1.0) carried over from provider-windows.json so that fact is not lost.

provider_limits.description: providers.<id>.limits entry (brief R4, 2026-09-27): one per model spelling. rpm/rpd/tpm/tpd are each optional non-negative ints; source is required (D20). MISTRALFIX (2026-09-28): the resolver reads rpm and plan_available too, not only tpm - `rpm: 0` (a zero request quota, measured 429) and `plan_available: false` (the model is not on this plan, measured 403) both mean the leg cannot serve, and tools/registry.py plan_dead_reasons() skips such a leg. plan_available must be a real boolean: the string 'false' is truthy at the gate, so rule 10 rejects a non-bool.

key_name.description: Additive field, not in spec 3.1 (brief MUSEAPI, 2026-09-27): the api-keys.yml entry this provider's key is read from, when it is not an entry named after the provider id. meta_api uses the user's existing 'meta' key (one Meta credential, two endpoints: the direct opencode provider and the OpenAI-compatible Model API gateway), so asking api-keys.yml for 'meta_api' would find nothing and skip the connection. Consumers: apply.sh/apply.ps1 (registration), tools/mirror-litellm-env.py (litellm/.env), tests/helpers/check-provider-registry.py (the sharing rule). It must name another provider's api-keys.yml name and two registered providers must never claim one name.

model_prefix.description: Additive field, not in spec 3.1 (brief AGYID, 2026-09-27): the prefix the live OmniRoute catalog serves this provider's models under when it differs from the provider's registry id. The antigravity OAuth bridge serves agy/* while registry legs keep antigravity/* (measured /v1/models 2026-09-27, source: inbox/L1-routing.md L0 live apply 11:44:31Z). Read only by tools/registry.py's gateway_ref() at render time; omniroute_id still names the provider connection apply.sh registers. Absent/null means the leg is emitted unchanged.

api_base.description: Public vendor endpoint only (registry.py check rejects private hosts/IPs/usernames, spec 3.1).

available.description: Additive field, not in spec 3.1: operator decision 2026-09-25 (OpenRouter not topped up) needs a way to mark a provider unusable without deleting or reordering its data - see routes.<id>.unavailable_legs for the matching per-leg flag. Omitted (not false) means available.

unavailable_until.description: Additive field, not in spec 3.1 (brief UNTIL 2026-09-26, skill rule R-gateway-12): time-bounded unavailability - the entry is unavailable until this UTC instant, then counts as available again on its own (the resolver's reason says 're-probe'; a multi-day quota reset never needs a hand edit to undo). Resolver-only: the renders and their CI drift gates never read it.

trains_on_prompts.description: Provider-level (spec 3.1), not per-model - a known simplification where one provider hosts both a training and a non-training leg; see mapping doc Open choices.

limits.description: Additive field, not in spec 3.1 (brief R4, 2026-09-27): per-model free-tier rate caps as data, keyed by the provider's own model spelling (the part of a leg after its '<provider>/' prefix). The resolver reads only `tpm` today (a request-size filter: need_tokens * 1.3 > tpm skips the leg); rpm/rpd/tpd are data only for now (no clock, no counters). Each value carries a source tag (D20). registry.py check rule 10 validates every key resolves via resolve_leg and every value is a non-negative int.

direct.description: the former llm-models.json direct-provider block: access that bypasses the OmniRoute gateway entirely (opencode's own provider catalog).

display_name.description: Additive field, not in spec 3.1: the former llm-models.json's human-readable 'name'. Kept so it is not lost (D9); routes carry their own per-surface display_name separately.

default_for.description: Additive field, not in spec 3.1: the former llm-models.json's opencode default-selection key (e.g. which api-key condition makes this model opencode's default). Kept so it is not lost (D9); it is an opencode.jsonc rendering concern, not consumed by the resolver.

family.description: anthropic/google/deepseek/meta/qwen/openai-oss/mistral/cohere/... (spec 3.1's list is open-ended; extra vendor families used here: nvidia, poolside, nex-agi, thinkingmachines, dots-studio, inclusionai, zhipu, moonshot, minimax, openrouter).

effort_ladder.description: Ordered rungs, e.g. ["none","low","medium","high","xhigh"]. Empty for a non-reasoning model.

paid_price_in.description: Additive field, not in spec 3.1: the post-free-cap price on the former llm-models.json entries that are free only under a cap (paid_input_price). Kept so the fact is not lost (D9); price_in/price_out stay the free-tier price.

client_bound.description: e.g. 'opencode' for the Zen free contributor leg, which 403s proxied traffic.

trains_on_prompts.description: Additive field, not in spec 3.1: an optional model-level override of providers.<id>.trains_on_prompts (PRIV brief, 2026-09-26), for a provider that hosts both a training and a non-training model (e.g. mistral-code-latest: true, on the otherwise non-training paid 'mistral' provider). Missing means inherit the provider's own value - see tools/registry.py's private_safe().

tier.description: Additive field, not in spec 3.1: an optional model-level override of providers.<id>.tier (PRIV2 brief, 2026-09-26), for a provider that hosts both a free/training pool and a paid, direct-key model under the same provider tier (e.g. the zen provider's own tier is 'free', but its opencode-zen/deepseek-v4.1-flash leg bills past the pool on the same key - the model-level override marks that leg 'paid'). Missing means inherit the provider's own value - see tools/registry.py's private_safe().

leg.description: provider/model: the part before the first '/' is a providers id or omniroute_id, the rest is a models id.

surface.description: One of routes.<id>.surfaces['omniroute'|'litellm'|'opencode'|'zed'|'openhands'] (spec 3.1: display name, context/output declared, effort default, OpenHands profile fields). Keyed by gateway (omniroute/litellm) here, per catalog/ide-models.json's own shape, with the exposing UI surfaces nested under 'clients' - see mapping doc Open choices.

context_declared.description: combos.json's coarse display string ('1M'/'128k'/'200k') for the omniroute surface - a picker/compaction convention, not the model's real window (see docs/models.md).

openhands_profile.description: configuration/openhands/tier-profiles.json fields for this surface (max_input_tokens, max_output_tokens, reasoning, and gateway/base_url when the profile bypasses the default gateway).

direct_profile.description: An OpenHands profile with no ide-models.json surface counterpart (e.g. the direct-OpenRouter spark profile with the full effort ladder).

unavailable_legs.description: Additive field, not in spec 3.1: operator decision 2026-09-25 (OpenRouter not topped up) marks the affected legs here by their exact routes.<id>.legs string, without removing or reordering them (spec 3.2 phase-1 equality gate).

unavailable_until.description: Time-bounded form of the flag (brief UNTIL 2026-09-26, R-gateway-12): the leg is unavailable until this UTC instant, then available again without a hand edit. Resolver-only; renders ignore it.

capabilities.description: SPAWNCAP (S2): what this client's headless mode can actually do. `run` refuses (exit 2) before dispatch when a task needs a capability the chosen client lacks; auto-choice skips clients that lack one. A split that is not measurable is recorded as both false, never guessed.

skills_dir.description: Null where the native skills directory is still unmeasured (plan Phase C5 spike).

signin_check.description: 'env:<NAME>' for a gateway client (presence check), the literal probe command for a client tools/autoos_clients.py already probes (agy), or null where no probe exists yet.

available.description: Additive field, not in spec 3.1 (brief UNTIL 2026-09-26): a client marked false is filtered out of routing; pair it with unavailable_until for a time-bounded outage so it comes back on its own.

unavailable_until.description: Additive field, not in spec 3.1 (brief UNTIL 2026-09-26, skill rule R-gateway-12): the client is unavailable until this UTC instant (e.g. a 429 quota reset), then counts as available again - the resolver's reason says 're-probe'. Resolver-only: renders and CI drift gates never read it.

policy.description: spec section 5: modes/theta/lambda (5.4), bucket table (5.2), effort rules (5.5), handoff caps (8.3), risk rules (5.7), seed priors and latency seed (5.6), verify/brief tokens (5.3). Every numeric value not itself part of a pinned data table (bucket_table) carries a source (D20).

modes.description: spec 5.4: theta (min success probability to pick a route) and lambda (USD per minute of wall clock) per mode.

bucket_table.description: The exact shape of tools/autoos_resolver.py DEFAULT_BUCKET_TABLE (spec 5.2), wrapped once with a source tag so the inner 'table' stays byte-identical for the resolver to load directly. tests keys are JSON-safe 'true'/'false' strings; a loader must convert them back to booleans before calling points()/bucket().

effort_rules.description: spec 5.5: first-matching-row table plus the reasoning-leg max_tokens floors.

free_client_models.description: SPAWNFREE (S2) item 1: the ordered free-model list a --free run falls through when its client prints a provider stop (tools/autoos-agent.py free_model_chain), keyed by client name. Values are the client's own model ids (opencode's zen free spellings), NOT registry leg ids - nothing here is checked against providers/models. Optional: a client with no entry runs the one --free-model it was given, as before.

free_concurrency.description: SPAWNFREE (S2) item 2: how many workers a free provider leg may serve at once on this host, keyed by the provider prefix of a free model id ('opencode/...' -> 'opencode'). A --free run at or above its cap waits for a slot instead of starting into a 429; tools/autoos-agent.py free_concurrency_cap defaults to 1 for an unlisted provider. Every leg is one shared account, so a cap below 1 would deadlock the queue.

handoff_caps.description: spec 8.3, keyed by orchestrator-model class. Each row carries a `match` list of lowercased model-id substrings (one entry per alias the row covers, or `["*"]` for the default) and a `window` (the family's context window in tokens).

match.description: lowercased substrings that pick a model id out for this row; `["*"]` is the default row.

window.description: the family's context window in tokens (spec 8.3).

risk_rules.description: spec 5.7: what auto-raises risk to high. Two rule shapes: a path glob matched against the card's declared paths, or a diff-shape trigger (a deletion anywhere in the diff).

leg_rules.description: Ordered list of fnmatch policy gates (Claude budget rules from briefs/common.md). Matched case-insensitively (pattern and leg are both casefolded), so a deny cannot be escaped by re-capitalising an id. First match wins; no match = allowed. A denied serving leg (not gated via routes.<id>.unavailable_legs) is an error.

reviewers.description: REVROUTE (S2) item 1, operator 2026-09-27T20:3xZ: the ordered preference list a review card walks -- WHO may review, as data rather than as a constant in the resolver. First usable entry wins: an entry is skipped when its `family` equals the author's (a review must come from a different model family), when the gateway/provider says it is unavailable, or when the card is privacy=sensitive and the model trains on prompts. `model` is the client's own model spelling (a gateway combo like 'omniroute/spark-1.3-contributor', or Haiku's client-side alias) -- like policy.free_client_models it is NOT checked against providers/models, because a reviewer is picked per client, not per route leg. `leg` (optional) names the registry leg that reviewer actually bills through, and is checked by rule 11: availability (providers.<id>.unavailable_until, which the spawner writes from a quota reset) and the privacy/training test are both read off it. A client-native reviewer with no gateway path (qoder, claude) carries no leg and is checked against `clients.<id>` alone -- which is also why it fails closed on sensitive work, since nothing says it does not train. `paid` is the operator's cost preference made visible: the paid Meta Muse contributor leads. `first_pass_only` true marks a reviewer that may take a normal-risk first pass but never closes (Claude Haiku); the high-risk Sonnet close is the resolver's own closer and is not on this list.
